thread:
sam: p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~480ms right after the 00:12 deploy. alerts fired. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/serving/latency?view=last_30m

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T00:12:03 UTC by sam — release/runtime-kernel-selector v2.4.1 applied to canary -> prod.

anya: saw the alert, looking. rolling metrics show a sharp rise in KV cache miss rate coincident with the deploy. not yet sure why kernel selector would affect cache locality but digging.

rafa: I pulled flamegraphs for a few p99 traces. looks like there are repeated cache invalidations and extra memcpy loops in the new kernel path. attaching snippet of hot trace: 
```
runtime:select_kernel(v2.4.1) -> aten_attention_fast_path
-- allocate temp buffer 64k
-- memcpy 64k x 12 loops
-- kv_cache.lock contended
```

kevin: can we revert the selector change to confirm? we should avoid user impact.

sam: +1 revert if easy. can we hotpatch?

anya: quick reproducer on a small seq length shows microbatch grouping changed: previous heuristic grouped by seq_len and model variant, new selector considers kernel throughput estimates and ends up creating larger microbatches with heterogeneous seqs -> increased KV cache churn.

rafa: here's the metric delta: KV cache hit rate went from 98.7% -> 84.2% for the affected pool; avg memcpy per request +1.8MB. p95 unchanged, p99 shot up. consistent with tail amplification.

kevin: sam do you want me to trigger rollback? I have the rollback script: `./ops/revert-release.sh runtime-kernel-selector v2.4.0`

sam: please rollback. label as high-priority incident. notify oncall SLO page.

deploy-bot: Rollback started by kevin at 2026-03-17T00:25:11 UTC. Target: runtime-kernel-selector v2.4.0.

ops-bot: Rolling revert: canary -> 50% -> 100%. autoscale unaffected. will post completion.

anya: while revert is running, I'm preparing a small patch to avoid grouping across model-variant boundaries. it's a conservative change: keep throughput-aware selection but require variant-homogeneous microbatches.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 2026-03-17T00:29:45 UTC. All nodes back to v2.4.0.

sam: p99 trending back down, KV hit rate recovering. good.

rafa: saved traces pre- and post-rollback. will upload to perf bucket: s3://perf-artifacts/1769462523-kernel-regressions/

kevin: thanks team. postmortem next steps: 1) add microbatch homogeneity constraint to kernel selector, 2) add synthetic test that simulates heterogeneous seq_len mixing and asserts KV hit rate, 3) add alert on kv_cache_miss_rate delta > 5% after deploy.

anya: noted. I'll open PR for the selector guard and the synthetic test. tagging @sam for review.

sam: make the PR and request fast-track. also update the release notes: revert and patch plan.

ops-bot: Incident closed: svc=runtime, severity=P2, duration=00:17:42, cause=kernel selector microbatching heuristic caused KV cache churn -> tail latency degradation.

kevin: small retrospective: throughput-only heuristics can hide cache-locality effects. we should profile kernel changes on cache-dense workloads before wide rollout.

anya: agree. adding a perf gate that runs a KV-cache heavy scenario during canary for 10 minutes.

sam: thanks everyone. filing follow-ups in runtime/infra board. :thumbsup:
